(Benefit)

As for its occurrence as a negation of what precedes it, as in: "I passed by a man, what a man (ayy rajul)!"

When ayy is shifted from interrogation into a description, the original form is "ayy rajul huwa," in the interrogative sense that is intended for magnification and awe.

It acquired this sense of magnification because they wish to show inability to encompass its description, so it is as if it were something whose true nature is asked about out of ignorance. Thus they placed it within the category of interrogation, which is designed for what is unknown.

Likewise came: ﴿The Striking Calamity! What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ and ﴿The Inevitable Reality! What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾

That is, its description cannot be fully encompassed. Since this expression has become established in the domain of magnifying and exalting a thing, it has come close to being a description, to the extent that they placed it in the category of the adjective (na't), and postponed it in its grammatical analysis (i'rab) from what precedes it.

Imam Ahmad said: "The moths (al-faraash) that fly around the lamp and get burned."

(Admonition)

They said: Also, the one who wrongs himself is the one whose scales are light and whose evil deeds outweigh his good, and the whole Qur'an indicates his loss and that he will not be saved, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then as for those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful. But as for those whose scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls because they had been, against Our signs, unjust.﴾ [al-A'raf: 8-9]

And His saying: ﴿But as for one whose scales are light, his refuge will be an abyss.﴾

So how could He mention His promise of His gardens and His honor to those who wronged themselves, whose scales are light?

And as-Siddiq (Abu Bakr) said in his testament to Umar: "Know that Allah has a right by night which He does not accept by day, and a right by day which He does not accept by night. And know that the scales of those whose scales become heavy only became heavy through their following the truth, and it was burdensome for them in the life of this world; and it is right that a scale in which the truth is placed should be heavy. And the scales of those whose scales become light on the Day of Resurrection only became light through their following falsehood in the life of this world, which was light for them; and it is right that a scale in which nothing but falsehood is placed should be light."
